tasks.spec:
BEHAVIOR - ISLAND BIRDWATCHING JOURNAL (charter queue T147: playability x self-doc) - window.GuildBirdJournal = { entries: {}, complete: false, open: false } with update/draw/__probe (probe returns { entries: count, complete, open }).
1. The proven pattern is tasks_out/worker_visitor.js (injected via include_files) - copy its conventions: self-installing ES module, no imports, no top-level DOM access (typeof guards), state object on a window global, update(now)/draw(ctx) hooks, __probe for testing. The client render loop auto-discovers your window.Guild* global and calls update/draw every frame when V.gameState === 'play'.
2. Client contract (all on window): V (V.gameState, V.workers, V.workerStates, V.weather, V.daylight 0..1, V.canvas, V.camera, V.grid), iso(gx, gy) -> {x,y}, fitText(text, maxW), window.GuildVisitor {gx, gy, moving, facing}, window.cue(name) optional sound hook (try/catch).
3. POCKET JOURNAL: pressing J toggles a small parchment journal panel (clipped, fitText discipline, gold #d4af37 header 'FIELD JOURNAL'). It tracks 5 fauna stamps: BIRDS (spot within 2 tiles of the NE aviary zone), BUTTERFLIES (E garden meadow), PIGEONS (courtyard), OWL (NE roost at night, V.daylight below 0.35), CAT (within 1.5 tiles of the sleeping guild cat). A stamp needs the visitor to stand in the right zone with the right conditions for 2 continuous seconds - then the page stamps in with a soft pop animation + cue('coin') in try/catch.
4. Each stamped entry shows a tiny pixel pictogram of the fauna (fillRect blocks, no images) + a one-line field note (write 1 flavor line per fauna). All 5 stamped = complete: a 3s confetti burst in gold + a one-line ceremony bubble ('MASTER BIRDER OF THE ISLAND') + cue('levelup').
5. Zone detection is by tile ranges you define (document them in a comment at the top); never write to V or other modules; zero exceptions if V/iso absent. No new accent colors - gold and parchment tones only. No persistence.
6. OUTPUT: only the new file, wrapped in one standard fenced code block (three backticks, no language tag). One line of prose max outside the fence.
